_comment: Writes the three timelines of the full product demo (under 5 minutes, no slides), Video.mp4 in Group19.zip: Part B. Generated by demo/make_timeline_demo.py; record with REPLAY_STEP_PACE=0.35.

steps.say: 09:40 · On the factory floor she has a phone, not a desk. The same home screen fits it.

steps.evaluate: await fetch('/__replay/clock?t=09:40'); const r = await fetch('/api/email/clock', {cache: 'no-store'}); window.threadpilotClock = await r.json(); window.threadpilotClockAnchor = performance.now();

steps.say: She taps the microphone and speaks. (The app is the real one; this recording simulates the microphone and speaker.)

steps.evaluate: window.__voiceSay = "where is o r d zero zero five";

steps.say: Spoken “O R D zero zero five” became ORD-005 and was sent. A spoken question gets a spoken answer.
The speaker button keeps spoken replies on for every answer, typed or spoken.

steps.evaluate: window.__voiceSay = "which customer has the most pieces in progress";

steps.say: A “most” question is computed from the order book, not guessed: Northwind Apparel, 8,000 pieces, and it says so aloud.

steps.evaluate: window.__voiceSay = "chase washing on o r d zero eight three";

steps.say: Actions work by voice too: a draft to washing about ORD-083. Still only a draft.
But a spoken “send now” is never sent. It waits in the box for a tap, so a misheard word cannot send an email.
Every page fits the phone: wide tables scroll inside their card, buttons are thumb-sized.
